prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell), Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System, serves Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone)/Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard)/Capacity Assessment Module/Slot Allocation Engine/Airport CDM Portal/Digital Briefing Room/Tower Sequence Manager/Ramp Movement Board/Departure Metering Service/Arrival Regulation Console/Contingency Operations Console/Flight Data Exchange/Surface Surveillance Adapter/Airline Interface Adapter/Alert Distribution Hub/Performance Analytics Warehouse/Audit Event Ledger/Identity Access Service/Business Rules Registry/Time Synchronization Service/Common Situation Display/Handling Resource Planner. Indicators: North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter/East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor/Sector Load Monitor/Gate Conflict Detector. Modes: Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase/Contingency Fallback State/Slot Compliance State. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin)/Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron)/Airline Operations Centre/Slot Coordinator/Aircraft Operator Representative/Network Operations Liaison/Meteorology Briefing Officer/Airport Duty Manager/Tower Supervisor/Ramp Control Lead/Ground Handling Dispatcher/Deicing Coordinator/Emergency Response Coordinator/System Support Engineer/Data Governance Steward/Airspace Sector Planner/Military Airspace Liaison. Airline operations centres submit Flight Intent Message via Adapter using Identity Access Service-authenticated accounts: preferred-route/departure-time/registration/turnaround/crew-readiness/passenger-connections. Adapter validates structure, maps carrier codes against Registry, forwards accepted intents to Exchange; rejects invalid/incomplete submissions with machine-readable reasons. Display shows proposed actions pending reconciliation. Prediction refines departure/arrival/recovery demand; Capacity compares Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate and qualifies confidence using Storm Cell Snapshot. Allocation produces Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time; airlines receive via Adapter/Portal. Ground Delay Program: Slot Coordinator applies published equity/feasibility rules; Copperfin confirms recovery priorities before revised constraints publish. Airlines assess crew-legality/rotation/maintenance/passenger-recovery; retime/cancellation/substitution/reroute require updated intents. Dispatcher sends Crew Bus Delay Slip; Planner correlates stand/baggage/catering/boarding. Gateway validates approved weather; invalid/late feeds remain degraded. Low-confidence forecasts remain visible; capacity provisional; below-threshold Hub alerts Copperfin/Tower

New part:
S142: The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to identify whether the proposed recovery action can be supported without creating surface congestion.
S143: The Tower Supervisor reviews metering effects in the Tower Sequence Manager when airline recovery actions change the expected departure order.
S144: The Airport Duty Manager monitors the Common Situation Display to ensure airline recovery decisions remain consistent with terminal capacity and passenger processing conditions.
S145: Disputed constraints are captured in the Collaborative Decision Log with the requesting airline, operational rationale, decision owner, and final resolution.
S146: During Adverse Weather Mode or a Capacity Reduction State, airline operations centres are expected to submit conservative intents that distinguish firm operating plans from speculative recovery options.
S147: During the Recovery Phase, the Regional Flow Platform permits more frequent intent updates while retaining the previous values needed for audit and performance review.
S148: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares submitted intents, issued constraints, actual off-block times, and achieved arrival outcomes to improve recovery playbooks.
S149: All airline integration transactions are time-stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and preserved in the Audit Event Ledger for post-operations reconstruction.
S150: The Airport CDM Portal provides the shared operational workspace where airport participants maintain a common view of departure readiness, arrival constraints, surface conditions, and slot impacts.
S151: For local voice coordination, the Airport CDM Portal is also known as Foxglove.
S152: Access to the Airport CDM Portal is controlled by the Identity Access Service so that each user sees only the workspaces, aircraft, stands, and decision records appropriate to the assigned role.
S153: The primary workspace presents the Common Situation Display with synchronized clocks, active operating state, airport demand, runway configuration, stand occupancy, and milestone status for each managed movement.
S154: The departure workspace is centered on Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, boarding readiness, aircraft servicing progress, and pushback coordination status.
S155: The arrival workspace shows expected landing demand, stand allocation risk, inbound regulation effects, and handling readiness indicators needed to protect the Airport Acceptance Rate.
S156: A dedicated milestone view records the planned, target, estimated, actual, and manually confirmed times for each turnaround event that affects a regulated departure or constrained arrival.
S157: The Airline Operations Coordinator is responsible for keeping the Flight Intent Message status, Target Off Block Time, passenger readiness indicator, and aircraft operational constraint notes current for each represented flight.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
